content.title: Protected banking content stays blocked after logout
content.intent: Prove that a page or control reached while authenticated does not remain usable as authenticated banking access after the user logs out and returns to previously visited protected content.
content.technique_notes: Techniques: auth + negative. Minted as a separate security path because AC-23 is a forbidden authenticated-access promise and revisiting previously reached protected banking content after logout changes the outcome from allowed to blocked. Representative persona: standard_user by equivalence partitioning from the documented full-access fixture at L61 and L73; the PRD does not define persona-specific logout behavior. Budget: owner selected no limit, so all 2 candidate scenarios were kept.

content.title: Authenticated user logs out cleanly
content.intent: Prove that a logged-in banking user can end the current authenticated session and leave the authenticated product state.
content.technique_notes: Techniques: eqp + state_flow. Used the standard_user full-access persona as the representative authenticated session because the PRD documents it as the normal/full-access experience and does not distinguish logout outcomes by persona. Kept as a distinct happy path to exercise the authenticated-to-logged-out state transition directly. Budget: owner selected no limit, so all 2 candidate scenarios were kept.

judgements.rationale: [applicability] Applied auth/negative techniques because the source defines logout as an authentication and protected-content boundary. Applied state_flow to the clean logout path because the use-case centers on changing from an authenticated state to a logged-out state.

[applicability] Did not mint boundary-value scenarios because the use-case exposes no ordered numeric, count, or length-constrained input in the source. Did not mint pagination, i18n, responsiveness, or API-contract scenarios because the logout evidence states no logout-specific promises in those families.

[applicability] Did not split scenarios by persona because the PRD states the actor as an authenticated user and gives no persona-specific logout rule; standard_user was the representative full-access authenticated equivalence class.
